comment: Every rendered verdict on this page carries data-verdict="<id>" and every rendered
measurement carries data-claim="<id>". Each id below is killed by at least one mutation
recorded here: a single-token edit to real source that forces the measured value the
other way.
A KILL IS DEFINED BY FOUR RULES, and scripts/mutate.mjs enforces all four:
1. the owning test PASSED unmutated, in the same run;
2. the patch actually CHANGED the file (anchor unique, bytes different);
3. the run served the MUTATED code -- proved two ways, because one is not enough:
the built bundle's hash must move, AND the failure must not match a shape that
means the code never ran at all (build error, server never started, nothing on
the port);
4. a patch that does not compile is DOES NOT BUILD and is never a kill.
`kills` names, per marker, the TEST and the exact CLAIM that kills it. That is not
documentation: e2e/global-teardown.ts requires each of those to have been OBSERVED
executing. expectVerdict/expectClaim record every (test, marker, claim) they run and
the rule is checked against that record, never against the spec's source text --
because a mention is not an assertion. See e2e/observations.ts.
The claim strings here were NOT TYPED. They were read out of the observation sink a
passing claims run wrote, for the same reason the `observed` evidence in
mutation-evidence.json is written by the runner rather than by a person.
e2e/verdict-coverage.spec.ts fails if the page renders a marker of either family that
no mutation covers, if a mutation names a marker the page never renders, or if a
mutation's `find` string no longer appears exactly once in its file (a rotted mutation
guards nothing).
Run them with: npm run test:mutation    (or: node scripts/mutate.mjs apply <id>)

name-match-inverted.find: if (matched) return { address: clean, matched: true, via: san, presented, wildcard }
name-match-inverted.replace: if (!matched) return { address: clean, matched: true, via: san, presented, wildcard }

promise-name.test: a failing name check names the actual cause

contains: A browser would refuse to go on

name-match-inverted.why: Flips the one RFC 6125 decision every name verdict reads, so an address the certificate is NOT for matches.

promise-time.test: an expired certificate says so, with the signatures still good

claim.contains: the only thing that changed is the date

validity-window-inverted.why: Inverts the validity-window test, so an expired certificate reports as in date.

signature-verify-inverted.find: return await child.verify({ publicKey: parent.publicKey }, webCrypto)

promise-vouched.test: one flipped bit turns the vouching verdict red and names why

claim.contains: Nobody in the trusted list vouched for it

link-0.test: one flipped bit turns the vouching verdict red and names why

padlock.test: 2. every verdict the page renders in that state reports success

signature-verify-inverted.why: Inverts the single WebCrypto signature check every chain link goes through. Also discharges 4.1d's requirement that breaking a check INSIDE the negative-claim fixture fails assertion 2.

promise-vouched.test: a self-signed leaf is rejected and the page says it signed itself

self-signed-accepted.why: A leaf that signed itself stops being named as such, so the page fails for a reason it cannot explain.

anchor-source.test: the root is reported as coming from the device, not the server

anchor-provenance-hidden.why: The root stops being reported as the device's own, which is the entire answer to promise 3.

padlock.test: 2. every verdict the page renders in that state reports success

alarm-reads-as-success.why: THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE. The brief requires the attacker certificate validating cleanly to read as ALARM and never as a green success; this makes it read green.

operator-identity-established.find:
outcome: 'not-established',
    headline: 'Not that the company is who it says',
operator-identity-established.replace:
outcome: 'pass',
    headline: 'Not that the company is who it says',

nonpromise-operator.test: 3. the limitation is on screen in that state, as the lab's own check

operator-identity-established.why: The lab's NEGATIVE CLAIM (4.1d), expressed as its own check returning 'not established'. This makes the check claim the operator WAS established.

nonpromise-honest.test: honesty is not established, and says so with every check passing

claim.contains: there is no field for it

honesty-established.why: Turns 'not that the site is honest' into a passing claim about honesty -- the exact misreading the lab exists to prevent.

nonpromise-sni.test: the hostname is readable in the bytes the page printed

sni-privacy-claimed.why: Claims hostname privacy the ClientHello printed below it visibly does not provide.

nonpromise-strength.test: the cipher list is unauthenticated NOW and checked later, both stated

cipher-strength-guaranteed.why: Claims the negotiation was authenticated when the same unprotected message carries it in the clear.

promise-key.test: the key check reports the curve the certificate actually carries

claim.contains: The certificate carries a usable key

key-check-failed.why: Inverts the WebCrypto key import that promise 1 now turns on. The check used to return 'pass' unconditionally, which made it the one asserted verdict on the page and gave it no reachable failure branch; this mutation is only possible because it is a measurement.

chain-length-off-by-one.find: text: `${a.path.steps.length} certificates in the walk, ${a.path.links.length} signatures checked.`,
chain-length-off-by-one.replace: text: `${a.path.steps.length + 1} certificates in the walk, ${a.path.links.length} signatures checked.`,

chain-length.test: the chain-length claim equals the boxes the page actually drew

claim.text: 4 certificates in the walk, 3 signatures checked.

chain-length-off-by-one.why: The counter stops agreeing with the boxes it counts -- the cross-check 4.1b asks for.

sni-readable.test: the hostname is readable in the bytes the page printed

sni-offset.test: the hostname is readable in the bytes the page printed

sni-offset-moved.why: Moves the declared position of the hostname by one byte. The claims suite finds where the name really is by searching the page's own printed bytes, so a wrong offset stops matching both the decode and the stated byte position.

negative-claim-weakened.find: 'A valid certificate does not establish who operates the name it was issued for.'
negative-claim-weakened.replace: 'A valid certificate confirms who operates the name it was issued for.'

negative-claim.test: 3. the limitation is on screen in that state, as the lab's own check

claim.contains: does not establish who operates the name

negative-claim-weakened.why: 4.1d requires that removing the negative-claim text fails assertion 3. Reversing it is the same test with a worse failure mode.

claim.contains: whether the checks pass or fail

all-checks-passed-ignores-expiry.why: Re-introduces the exact bug this lab shipped and then fixed: the every-check-passed value ignoring the expiry check, so the page read NO PADLOCK at the top and 'Every check above passed' a few hundred pixels down. A page that contradicts itself teaches whichever half the reader read, and nothing caught it because the honesty row was only asserted in the state where every check really does pass.
